raw_resume.summary: B.Tech Computer Science and Engineering graduate (2025) who builds full-stack web applications with Java, Spring Boot and React. Seeking a Software Development Engineer role to apply strong fundamentals in object-oriented design and algorithms to scalable systems.

projects.name: PaySplit - Group Expense Settlement
projects.description: Built a Spring Boot REST API and React TypeScript frontend to split shared expenses and process payments. Integrated Razorpay webhooks for payment state transitions, wrote 40 JUnit tests, and containerised the application with Docker.

projects.name: Campus Library Reservations
projects.description: Designed a Java and Spring Boot service with MySQL schema for study room bookings. Piloted with 120 students over 2 weeks and eliminated double-booking conflicts.

projects.name: Order Tracker Dashboard
projects.description: Developed a React and TypeScript dashboard consuming a REST API to display order status in real time, deployed locally with Docker Compose.

profile_improvement_tips: Gain hands-on experience with data structures (linked lists, trees, graphs, hash tables) and algorithm design (sorting, searching, dynamic programming) through coding practice on platforms like LeetCode or HackerRank, then highlight this in a dedicated 'Algorithms & Data Structures' project or in project descriptions.

Study and apply object-oriented design principles (SOLID, design patterns) explicitly in your projects; document how your PaySplit or Library Reservations service uses inheritance, polymorphism, or design patterns, and name these in project bullets.

Build or contribute to a distributed systems project (e.g. a microservices architecture, message queue integration, or multi-node system) to demonstrate understanding of scalability, consistency, and fault tolerance — this is a core JD requirement.
raw_resume.growth_note: You are a strong fresher with solid full-stack fundamentals, but the JD emphasises data structures, algorithms, distributed systems and object-oriented design — areas not yet evident in your profile. Gaining explicit experience in these will significantly improve your fit.
